title: Accept 30002170: A localized Gaussian-witness lower bound for fractional iterated area on uniform grids
body:
## Accepted result and published preprint

**A localized Gaussian-witness lower bound for fractional iterated area on uniform grids**, Alec Kriebel. Published paper and verification package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23430906 (https://zenodo.org/records/23430906).

For independent standard fractional Brownian components with the same fixed H in (1/4,1), this note gives a localized Gaussian-witness proof that every square-integrable estimator of the canonical iterated integral integral_0^T B^1 dB^2, based on both complete uniform grids, has RMS error at least c_H T^(2H)n^(1/2-2H), with an explicit positive H-only constant, for every T>0 and integer n>=1. Brownian exact optimal error and smooth asymptotic rate are prior results. Local Fourier covariance bumps and Gaussian projection have established antecedents. Historical theorem and method priority, full novelty, and worldwide current-open status remain UNKNOWN; the inspected primary controls did not contain a matching rough conditional lower theorem. Canonical-area existence and sufficient L2 convergence are the external inputs; exact Euler coefficients of the pinned NTU arXiv v1 are not endorsed. No sharp constant, exact limit, endpoint, H-uniform, nonuniform/adaptive, unequal-H or correlated-component claim is made. Prepared with extensive AI assistance; unrefereed and not formally certified. Preparation and later-review status are recorded in STATUS.json and the dated preparation reports.

## Accepted scope and review

For every H∈(1/4,1), T>0, n≥1 and independent standard fractional Brownian components, every square-integrable estimator based on both components at jT/n has RMS error≥c_H T^(2H)n^(1/2-2H) for the canonical ∫B1dB2, c_H>0.

No original lower-bound-target gap asserted. Rough range (1/4,1/2) is candidate new residual; Brownian optimum and smooth-range asymptotic rate are credited. No sharp constant, normalized limit, endpoints, arbitrary mesh or adaptive sampling claimed.

The result is accepted at the exact audited head `fc37aa5169a0fe6adae0a254c9ee6c1531a2911f`. 5 fresh independent complete AI whole-package reviews were completed, with the final review finding zero actionable issues. Subsequent bounded administrative adoption is recorded in the current external ROOT final seal; earlier status/counter/hold fields remain dated history. Prior mathematical results and proof dependencies are credited. Historical novelty and worldwide current openness are unestablished. AI tools were used extensively; this is an unrefereed preprint, without conventional human peer review or formal proof certification.

The repository Zenodo uploader verified the exact reviewed metadata and PDF/support bytes. The Google Workspace CLI recorded the DOI/details in the requested tracker with exact read-back. No GitHub release is created. Current audit and publication receipts: `audits/pr1071_30002170`.

## Accepted full original lower-bound target

Problem 30002170 / OWR-12013-003, first substantive approach 1/5. The original lower-bound target is accepted after independent AI mathematical audit and acceptance review: for every fixed H in (1/4,1), every T>0 and every integer n>=1, the optimal conditional-expectation RMS error for the canonical iterated integral is at least c_H T^(2H) n^(1/2-2H), with c_H>0 depending only on H. Both independent standard fractional Brownian components are observed at every uniform sample time. The proof applies to every square-integrable observation-measurable estimator.

The rough range 1/4<H<1/2 is the substantive residual. The exact Brownian optimum and smooth-range asymptotic optimal rate remain credited known cases. No historical novelty/priority certificate, sharp constant, exact normalized-error limit, endpoint result, or adaptive/arbitrary-mesh extension is claimed.

## Complete proofs and mathematical audit

The edition preserves the complete localized Gaussian-witness proof, its all-H extension, the full Euler-to-polygonal canonical-convention proof, and the full independent mathematical audit. The audit retains all essential reasoning, including Fourier normalization, regularity and periodization, independence from both sampled components, signed-PSD-trace variance control, finite-identity/L2 passage, and joint-law transfer from the auxiliary Gaussian realization. Every displayed formula in these four mathematical documents is preserved byte for byte. No mandatory mathematical repair was needed.

Candidate/pending status is updated to scoped full-target acceptance. All material is AI-assisted and unrefereed; acceptance is not external human peer review or formal proof-assistant certification. The explicitly identified established area-convergence theorem and standard Gaussian/Fourier foundations remain inputs.
